clue.text: Recalled as a bird once in the Pacific

indicators.note: called back, so the little word as is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the moa was a giant flightless New Zealand bird, now extinct

explanation.surface: Someone remembers a bird that used to live in the Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' turns AS into SA; the moa supplies the rest. The definition is loose: the answer is an island nation located in the Pacific.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is an island nation lying in the South Pacific Ocean.

clue.text: Uttered in no childish way

parts.note: said with adult firmness, the way a grown man would talk, an old expression of approval for brave words

explanation.surface: Someone speaks in a mature, grown-up manner.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase praises words said with courage and maturity, the opposite of a boy's speech.

clue.text: Tree also wild olive

indicators.note: running wild means the letters of the two words are scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: A botanist notes that a certain tree is also known as the wild olive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' looks part of the definition 'wild olive', but it is the anagram signal working on TREE and ALSO.
explanation.definitionFit: The oleaster, Elaeagnus, is a shrub or small tree with olive-like fruit, often called wild olive.

clue.text: Old instrument carried in bag provided

parts.note: a sack is a large bag
but in the old sense 'unless' or 'only if', a conditional like provided

explanation.surface: An antique instrument is carried in a bag supplied for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carried in' is padding for the surface; the two pieces simply sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A sackbut is the Renaissance forerunner of the trombone.

clue.text: Sum up speech from a report garbled by Edward initially

indicators.note: a garbled message has its parts mixed up, so these letters are rearranged
initially means take only the opening letter of the following name

explanation.surface: Edward muddles a report while trying to summarise a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'garbled' rearranges A REPORT into PERORAT; Edward's first letter E finishes it.
explanation.definitionFit: To perorate is to deliver the concluding, summarising part of an oration.

clue.text: Songs of the foreign sea for businessmen

parts.note: mer is French for the sea
chants are songs, especially simple repeated ones

explanation.surface: Sea shanties sung abroad are offered as entertainment for traders.
explanation.definitionFit: Merchants are traders who buy and sell goods.

clue.text: From whence came a miss touring Majorcan resort?

indicators.note: going around, so the girl's word encloses the resort

parts.note: a miss is a young unmarried woman, a lass
Palma is the capital and main resort of Majorca

explanation.surface: Where did that girl come from who has been travelling round a Majorcan resort?
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole question's opening: the answer is a place someone comes from. The city is in the Canary Islands, though the resort inside it is Majorcan.
explanation.definitionFit: The question asks for a place of origin, and the answer is a city in Gran Canaria.

clue.text: Be go-ahead, unlike Lot's wife

definitions.meaning: to be enterprising and keep moving forward without regrets
in Genesis Lot's wife turned to glance at Sodom and became a pillar of salt

explanation.surface: Be enterprising and do not do what Lot's wife did.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means pressing on without regret, the opposite of Lot's wife, who turned round and was punished.

clue.text: Trap for male she harassed

indicators.note: harassed means troubled and agitated, so the three letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A woman who was pestered sets a trap for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A mesh is a net, used for catching things.

clue.text: See 8
The Beethoven No. 3 a girl hungers for

definitions.text: The Beethoven No. 3 a girl hungers for

parts.words: The Beethoven No. 3 a girl hungers for
parts.note: the symphony's title is Italian for brave and valiant, and a romantic young woman longs for a valiant champion

explanation.surface: A girl yearns for Beethoven's Third Symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a girl craving music; the title of Beethoven's Third also suggests the gallant man she yearns for.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's Symphony No. 3 is known by this Italian title meaning heroic.

clue.text: Being acceptable, can return to a group

parts.note: U means socially acceptable, upper-class usage

indicators.note: coming back, so the word for can is read backwards

parts.note: a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Being suitable, a can is sent back to a group.
explanation.walkthrough: U for acceptable is the old upper-class versus non-U distinction of British speech; 'return' reads the can word backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single group forming part of a larger body, as in a military unit.

clue.text: Disturbance caused by a volcanic eruption?

definitions.meaning: a sudden violent change or upset
literally the ground being heaved upwards, as when magma forces its way out

explanation.surface: A volcano erupts and causes turmoil.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a violent disruption, and literally a lifting of the earth's crust.

clue.text: The Great Barrier? Takes real force to shift it

indicators.note: shifting the letters moves them into a new order

explanation.surface: Moving the Great Barrier would take a great deal of force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Great Barrier' is the Great Barrier Reef off Queensland, Australia; 'to shift' rearranges REAL and FORCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia's Great Barrier is the world's largest system of living marine polyps.

clue.text: Tricks that Rigoletto got up to

definitions.text: Tricks that Rigoletto got up to

parts.words: Tricks that Rigoletto got up to
parts.note: Rigoletto, in Verdi's opera, is the court jester, so his pranks are a jester's antics

explanation.surface: An opera character's mischief is described.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means silly or clownish behaviour, the stock in trade of a court jester.

clue.text: See 2
Casts off sometimes on sale?

definitions.meaning: factory seconds with flaws are often sold cheaply

explanation.surface: Discarded items sometimes turn up for sale.
explanation.definitionFit: To reject is to discard, and rejects are imperfect goods sometimes sold at a discount.

clue.text: Minute hour-glass used for crackers

parts.note: a tiny sand-glass timing a few minutes, used when boiling things you crack open at breakfast

explanation.surface: A tiny hour-glass is used when making crackers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' reads as the unit of time but means tiny; the 'crackers' are the things that get cracked.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sand-glass times the boiling of breakfast eggs.

clue.text: Glacial deposit a harbinger of further precipitation, one hears

indicators.note: tells us the answer is how the phrase sounds when spoken, not how it is spelt

parts.note: a sign of yet more rain to come

explanation.surface: A glacial deposit is said to signal more bad weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Moraine is the rock and debris a glacier carries and leaves behind.

clue.text: Sailor with a Milne character is a newcomer to Australia

parts.note: a jack, or Jack Tar, is a sailor
Roo is the baby kangaroo in A. A. Milne's Winnie-the-Pooh

explanation.surface: A sailor accompanied by a Pooh character arrives new to Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian slang for a young trainee on a sheep or cattle station, new to outback life.

clue.text: File on right twister

parts.note: an asp is a snake, something that twists and coils

explanation.surface: A file is kept on the right-hand side of a twisting road.
explanation.definitionFit: A rasp is a coarse file for shaping wood or metal.

clue.text: Academic wear perhaps, albeit grand to possess

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds
to own is to possess

explanation.surface: Academic dress might be a grand thing to have.
explanation.definitionFit: Academics and graduates wear a long robe at ceremonies.

clue.text: Swears it could be the fish

indicators.note: suggests a different arrangement of the same letters might give the answer

explanation.surface: Someone curses, perhaps at a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrasse is a brightly coloured sea fish.

clue.text: Light garb to take off

definitions.meaning: sports kit, a team's lightweight outfit

explanation.surface: Light clothing is easy to remove.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip is a team's kit, and to strip is to undress.

clue.text: Intervals cuemen appreciate

definitions.meaning: snooker players value long scoring runs at the table

explanation.surface: Snooker players enjoy the intervals in a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaks are pauses, and in snooker a break is a sequence of pots by one player.

clue.text: Carroll's heroine gets sort of brown in a Spanish town

indicators.note: Alice gets something inside her, taking the colour word into her name

parts.note: Alice is the heroine of Lewis Carroll's Wonderland books

indicators.note: a sort of version of the word, its letters rearranged

parts.note: tan is a shade of brown

explanation.surface: Alice picks up a suntan while staying in a Spanish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' says the colour word is rearranged, and 'gets ... in' says Carroll's heroine takes it inside her name.
explanation.definitionFit: Alicante is a port and resort on Spain's Costa Blanca.

clue.text: One of Lear's brood proving a loss to a President

indicators.note: the letter is lost from the name, removed from it

parts.note: Ronald Reagan was the 40th US President

explanation.surface: One of King Lear's daughters turns out to be a loss to a president.
explanation.definitionFit: Regan is one of King Lear's three daughters in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Covered by a sheet in a boat at sea?

parts.note: beneath something means under it
poetically a sail is a sheet of canvas

explanation.surface: Someone lies under a bedsheet aboard a boat at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel moving by wind power is said to be travelling with canvas up.
